    Finite-representable coordinates on projective modules #

    When the representing objects have local endomorphism rings, every indecomposable projective finite module is a covariant representable. Finite indecomposable decomposition therefore puts every projective finite module in literal finite-representable coordinates. Applying this to projective covers produces exact minimal two-step presentations in the matrix model used by the Nakayama push-down comparison.
